title: Command-line data path causing backups to fail
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing open and closed issues

### Current Behavior

In my environment I run Sonarr specifying a data dir on the command line, for example `/usr/bin/open /Applications/Sonarr.app --args /nobrowser -data=$APP_HOME/appdata/Sonarr/`.

When elements of my environment changed, $APP_HOME ended up expanding to a directory with a trailing slash, so the the parameter became `-data=/opt/example//appdata/Sonarr/`.

Most Sonarr features work just fine, but I noticed that backups started failing, and looking at the debug logs, other file-handling features were too. The backups were trying to back up the non-existent config file `/opt/example/appdata/Sonarrr/config.xml`. Note the single slashes and three Rs in Sonarrr.

Please note this is a duplicate of [Radarr issue 11300](https://github.com/Radarr/Radarr/issues/11300).

### Expected Behavior

I'd expect Sonarr's backups to work with a config file path like /opt/example//appdata/Sonarr/config.xml

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start Sonarr using a command-line parameter to specify the data dir with multiple slashes within the path (not the final path separator). For example, `-data=/opt/example///appdata/Sonarr/` but not `-data=/opt/example/appdata/Sonarr///`.
2. In the System menu select the Backup page.
3. Click 'Backup Now' to initiate a manual backup.

The backup will fail and the log/debug log will show that the backup file failed because the malformed config file path couldn't be found.

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: macOS Sequoia 15.7.2
- Sonarr: 4.0.16.2944
- Docker Install: No
- Using Reverse Proxy: No
- Browser: n/a
- Database: Sqlite 3.36.0
```

### What branch are you running?

Develop

### Trace Logs

[over-slashed-directory-trace-log-for-sonarr](https://gist.github.com/Touchstone64/adfdcdfaa433414a596dcb95062af410)

### Anything else?

Please note this is a duplicate of [Radarr issue 11300](https://github.com/Radarr/Radarr/issues/11300).

comments.body: why not just sanitize the data argument + fail when users pass invalid paths. vs trying to chase down any path thats used down the line to do a hacky fixup? then your PR looks to contain unexpected changes unrelated to this issue
